key_insight: AI-generated synthetic data in biomedicine grew rapidly from 2015–2025, but real-world deployment lagged far behind the publication boom.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic data may help expand biomedical research and training data, yet its clinical value depends on stronger evaluation, reporting, and translation into practice.
method: Systematic mapping of 4,143 papers published between 2015 and 2025
Bibliometric analysis with expert annotation plus LLM-assisted classification
Grouped studies by modality, medical domain, paper type, deployment status, and research stance
evidence_signal: The review found continuous publication growth, but only 27 papers reported operational use and critical studies stayed below 1%, highlighting a large evidence-to-deployment gap.
watch_item: The field may be overrepresented by supportive preclinical work, so deployment claims should be treated cautiously without stronger validation and standard reporting.
paper_title: AI-Based Synthetic Data in Biomedicine: A Decade of Growth and a Persistent Translation Gap
